{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABc8CA8A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhGeIuY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 107, "title": "Rebalance browser CI shards and reduce test execution cost without losing coverage", "body": "## Problem

The current **main** browser validation is red after merging PR #106 / Issue #105, even though the corresponding PR head passed all checks. The failure is a **browser shard timeout**, not an identified emulator correctness regression.

Concrete evidence:
- Failed main workflow: [Browser Pages run 42160464316](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/42160464316), commit `4ffcb97c6f028def7da1085ebee21bce9ee6b959` (2026-11-06).
- `native`, `wasm`, and `browser (shared)` succeeded. `browser (scenarios)` failed and therefore the mandatory aggregate `build` gate failed; publication was skipped, correctly.
- The scenario runner reported `BROWSER_TOTAL {"shard":"scenarios","ms":1199608,"status":"failed","groups":42,"expected":43}`, then `timeout=true` and `CI_TIMING {"stage":"browser-scenarios","seconds":1200.237,"exit_code":1}`. `scspMvol` was the active group when the worker was terminated at the 20-minute compact-transport cap; it is **not proven that the test's assertions failed**. `largeMedia` was not completed. The `Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await` during forced teardown is a consequence to investigate only if it also reproduces *without* the timeout.
- Passing PR workflow on the earlier PR head: [run 42157801981](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/42157801981). This pass does not establish that main's workload has adequate runtime margin.

The failed scenario log measured these individual groups at approximately: `cdRuntime` 219.7 s, `externalDiscovery` 188.3 s, `chd` 132.1 s, `mosaic` 128.1 s, `rotationHighResolution` 100.6 s, `videoTransactions` 88.6 s, plus `cdStream` 48.2 s. The six largest alone consumed ~857 s. These are **observed samples**, not fixed performance guarantees. A previous shard rebalance was needed in Issues #93 and #103; the suite has grown and again lacks reliable headroom.

## Expected outcome

Restore a **fully green mandatory main workflow** with meaningful runtime headroom, while reducing *actual* test execution cost where evidence supports safe improvements. Both independent browser shards must retain complete, independently verified regression coverage and deterministic failure propagation. Balance the two shards using real measured work rather than merely raising timeout limits, blindly moving expensive modules, or hiding expensive checks.

This is a **CI/test execution optimization task**, not an emulator feature change. Follow [CI test/performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/ci-performance.md#test-and-ci-principles): prefer the lightest useful layer, eliminate redundant execution, retain meaningful device/guest/Wasm/Canvas/AudioWorklet coverage and exact revision/artifact gates. Target <10-minute normal CI feedback (8-minute stretch) as an **investigation goal**, not a hard acceptance gate or excuse to skip tests.

## Investigation and implementation guidance

1. Establish comparable current-head baseline from the failing main log, the passing PR log, both shard manifests and the timing/operation instrumentation. Quantify per-group elapsed time and, when available, CPU, browser/Wasm call counts, expensive `run_steps` / `advance_frame` loops, repeated setup, PCM/media transfers, and memory pressure. Explain uncertainty due to hosted-run variation. Do not infer host CPU time from elapsed time.
2. **Rebalance** `scripts/browser-shards.json` conservatively, preserving the ordered shared Play/UI trace and independently isolated scenario contexts. Candidates worth *measuring* include moving the independent `chd` (~132 s) and `cdStream` (~48 s) groups to `shared`, **only if measured shared headroom and any context/order constraints justify it**. Alternatively choose a better partition from measured totals. Retain both-shard coverage and <=2 concurrent browser workers; no duplicate tests or dropped group.
3. **Reduce total work, not just redistribute it.** Profile the high-cost modules (`scripts/cd-runtime.mjs`, `scripts/external-discovery.mjs`, `scripts/chd.mjs`, `scripts/mosaic.mjs`, `scripts/rotation-high-resolution.mjs`, `scripts/video-transactions.mjs`, plus `scripts/scsp-mvol.mjs`) and the native/browser driver. Find redundant duplicate guest runs/fixtures/setup or unnecessary JS↔Wasm/browser round trips. Prefer consolidating equivalent assertions or moving suitable arithmetic/combination checks to existing native tests when the native test independently preserves defect detection. Optimize test driver/fixture reuse, deterministic chunking, and measurement overhead if appropriate. If a guest-clock/repetition reduction is justified, explain exactly which bugs/timing boundaries remain detectable; **never alter a required hardware deadline, expected pixel/audio/IRQ/guest result, or remove a unique negative control solely to meet the limit**. Report total-work reduction separately from scheduling gains.
4. Preserve existing `scripts/browser-groups.json` registry and full group inventory (currently **74 total**; 33 shared incl. setup, 41 scenarios previously before current growth; consult *actual* manifests). Test counts and mappings must be derived from current source, not copied from past records. Keep explicit all-group coverage in normal CI and the existing serial/debug/targeted run capability.
5. Respect `scripts/browser-suite.mjs`'s existing 1,200 s compact/3,600 s raw worker timeouts, cancellation/forced teardown semantics, runner regression tests and the required aggregate build gate. **Do not solve this by increasing timeouts, adding retries, ignoring failed jobs, allowing missing reports, reducing assertion strictness, changing reported statuses or expanding runner capacity without measured justification.** If later evidence supports a timeout change, document it as a distinct justified proposal.
6. After optimization, run the full unchanged-coverage browser suite and the repository-required native/Wasm/fixture/runner tests as applicable. Collect timings for **both** shards and costly groups with consistent environment/build. Verify a passed hosted PR workflow on the exact final head (native, Wasm, shared, scenarios, build), and record a substantial observed margin to 1,200 seconds on both shards; explain if only local evidence exists. CI must genuinely run all groups, including `scspMvol` and `largeMedia`. Re-run a complete browser validation if necessary to assess variance, without making live Pages deployment or human confirmation a pre-merge gate.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A root-cause/critical-path report identifies the failing hosted run, timeout limit, incomplete group(s), passing controls, baseline per-shard and per-group timing, and explicitly separates timeout from functional assertion failure.
- [ ] An evidence-based shard rebalance avoids the observed 20-minute scenario overload, preserves isolation and dependencies and leaves adequate **measured** headroom in **both** shards (do not just shift the same timeout into shared).
- [ ] At least one substantive, justified **test-work reduction** is implemented **if a safe candidate is demonstrated**; otherwise publish a bounded profiling result with the rejected candidates and retain the same workload without inventing savings. Report before/after total browser worker time and individual major groups, separately from end-to-end elapsed and summed runner time.
- [ ] All required tests and genuinely distinct regression cases remain covered: original reset-vector guests, hardware timing/IRQ/DMA, HLE/BIOS/media formats, Canvas, WebAudio/AudioWorklet/SCSP/MVOL, multi-shard operation and native/Wasm cross-validation. No removal of a distinct assertion/negative control to make the suite green.
- [ ] The browser inventory/manifest, ordered shared trace, fresh scenario contexts, expected-result checks, failure and cancellation propagation, timeout behavior, report integrity, exact revision and tested-Wasm-asset digest, and aggregate publication gate remain correct. Add/update runner coverage for the new shard assignment and verify that missing/failed groups cannot pass.
- [ ] Applicable fmt/build/tests/Clippy, fixture reproduction, production Wasm build, runner regressions, full browser suite and exact-head hosted PR CI are successful. Record actual commands, results and timing data. Never claim a local run is hosted success.
- [ ] Update `docs/ci-performance.md` (and a scoped validation record if useful) with the baseline, measured improvements, retained coverage, remaining costs and any still-unverified hosted variability. Keep the change as small as practical.

## Optional validation

Multiple independently repeated hosted full-suite runs to characterize performance variance; extra performance profiling/CPU/RSS sampling; production Pages check after merge. Not gates unless evidence demonstrates an actual regression.

## Required post-merge verification

None specified. Green hosted PR CI on the final head is required pre-merge; a future main deployment may still depend on the normal main-only workflow.
